Roads are a dict keyed by road id with a \"status\" field. Current statuses: R-03=\"R\", R-08=\"X\", R-09=\"R\", R-12=\"X\", R-13=\"R\"; all others \"A\". E.g. RT-02 (WH-NVL-03->SITE-NVL-B, 22km) uses blocked R-03 while RT-03 (31km) is open; RT-05 (WH-CPL-05->SITE-CPL-B, 18km) uses closed R-08 while RT-06 (26km) uses restricted R-09; RT-07 (WH-HGL-07->SITE-HGL-A, 20km) uses closed R-12 while RT-08 (27km) is open; RT-09 (WH-HGL-07->SITE-HGL-B) uses restricted R-13 only.", "file": "data/network.json"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "notifications/sms.py: TEMPLATES[\"DELIVERY_MOVED\"] = \"Lifeline: road closures. Deliveries carry route_id and vehicle fields (core/models.py Delivery).", "file": "distribution/planner.py"}, {"id": "R10", "statement": "logistics/routes.py also has sites_served(warehouse_id: str, network: dict | None = None) -> list[str] returning sorted unique sites with a route from the warehouse — a model for the name-ordering required in rerouted_sites.", "file": "logistics/routes.py"}, {"id": "R11", "statement": "Note on semantics: per the access.py docstring, both \"R\" (restricted) and \"X\" (closed) are described as closed to ALL vehicles, so under the documented rules no vehicle may pass a non-\"A\" road; VEHICLE_WEIGHT (truck=heavy, van=light) exists in access.py and may be intended to differentiate vehicles for restricted roads, but the docstring as written gives no light-vehicle exception.", "file": "logistics/access.py"}]}}
